title: WORKSHEET 17
subject: Future Perfect / Future Perfect Continuous
subjectVi: Ngữ pháp bài 17: Future Perfect / Future Perfect Continuous

sections.instruction: What will life be like in the year 2100? Complete the sentences using WILL HAVE + PAST PARTICIPLE form: (Example: By 2100, the world’s population will have increased (increase) to around 30,000 million.)

questions.prompt: Life [gap] (become) more automated by then.
questions.explanation: future perfect: will have + past participle

questions.prompt: Computers [gap] (take over) many of the jobs that people do today.
questions.explanation: future perfect: will have + past participle

questions.prompt: The earth’s supplies of oil, coal and gas [gap] (run out).
questions.explanation: future perfect: will have + past participle

questions.prompt: [gap] (scientists / find) other sources of energy?
questions.explanation: question: will + subject + have + past participle

questions.prompt: How [gap] education [gap] (change)?
questions.explanation: question: will + subject + have + past participle

questions.prompt: [gap] (we / find) a way to feed all the people in the world?
questions.explanation: question: will + subject + have + past participle

sections.instruction: Use WILL HAVE + PAST PARTICIPLE form:

questions.prompt: Tom and Ann are going to the cinema. The film begins at 7.30 and it is already 7.20. And it will take them 20 minutes to get there. When they get there, [gap] (the film / already / start).
acceptedAnswers: the film will already have started|the film will have already started
questions.explanation: future perfect: completed before a future time

questions.prompt: Jim always goes to bed at 11 o’clock. Tom is going to visit him at 11.30 this evening. When Tom arrives, [gap] (Jim / go / to bed).
acceptedAnswers: Jim will have gone to bed
questions.explanation: future perfect: completed before a future time

questions.prompt: Tom is on holiday. He has very little money and he is spending too much too quickly. Before the end of his holiday, [gap] (he / spend / all his money).
acceptedAnswers: he will have spent all his money
questions.explanation: future perfect: completed before a future time

questions.prompt: Chuck came to Britain from the US nearly three years ago. Next Monday it will be exactly three years since he arrived. Next Monday [gap] (he / be / here / exactly three years).
acceptedAnswers: he will have been here for exactly three years|he will have been here exactly three years
questions.explanation: future perfect + for: duration up to a future time

questions.prompt: Next year is Ted and Amy’s 25th wedding anniversary. They [gap] (be married) for 25 years.
questions.explanation: future perfect + for: duration up to a future time

questions.prompt: Jane is from New Zealand. She is traveling around Europe at the moment. So far she has traveled about 1,000 miles. By the end of the trip, [gap] (she / travel) more than 3,000 miles.
acceptedAnswers: she will have traveled|she will have travelled
questions.explanation: by + future time → future perfect

questions.prompt: By next February I [gap] (write) my third book.
questions.explanation: by + future time → future perfect

questions.prompt: I hope you [gap] (not / forget) my name by tomorrow.
questions.explanation: negative: won't have + past participle

questions.prompt: By next week we [gap] (redecorate) the house.
questions.explanation: by + future time → future perfect

questions.prompt: Next July she [gap] (be) dead for ten years.
questions.explanation: future perfect + for: duration up to a future time

questions.prompt: I hope I [gap] (not / make) a lot of mistakes in this exam when I finish it.
questions.explanation: negative: won't have + past participle

questions.prompt: By the end of this year I [gap] (drive) more than one hundred thousand kilometers with this car.
questions.explanation: by + future time → future perfect

questions.prompt: I hope it [gap] (stop) raining before the match starts.
questions.explanation: future perfect: completed before a future event

questions.prompt: I [gap] (have) an operation when you come back.
questions.explanation: future perfect: completed before a future event

questions.prompt: By this time next week I [gap] (marry).
acceptedAnswers: will have married|will have got married|will have gotten married|will have been married
questions.explanation: by + future time → future perfect

questions.prompt: If nothing is done one million species that are alive today [gap] (become) extinct in twenty years.
questions.explanation: future perfect: completed within a future period

questions.prompt: The tropical rain forests [gap] (disappear) in thirty years.
questions.explanation: future perfect: completed within a future period
